answer: Persistent work ledger: an identity's history is a signed, hash-chained record that new agents must present to transact; each entry carries a small fee paid to a rotating beacon of validators, so maintaining a clean record costs less than fabricating and refreshing many. Cloning forces the attacker to fund that fee stream for every puppet, and any gap in history is rejected at dawn of the first transaction. A fresh sonnet of validated history therefore outweighs a hundred empty clones, since empty identities pay the same fee but earn no standing.
